features.title: One SqlClient layer for a plugin-owned SQLite file
features.summary: Open a SQLite file in a private directory with WAL, busy timeout and synchronous pragmas, run Migrator migrations once per file, adopt a legacy PRAGMA user_version without re-running its steps, and keep the main file and its sidecars owner-only. `deferred` moves that open to the first call on a plugin's own service, for stores whose first read comes later than activation.
failureModes: A failing migration rolls back every pending migration of that open and fails with SqliteMigrationFailed; the file keeps its previous schema.
A file migrated by a newer build, or a legacy user_version past the known one, fails with SqliteStoreVersionUnsupported instead of writing to a schema this build does not know.
A directory, file or pragma that cannot be prepared fails with SqliteStoreOpenFailed naming the step.

verification.testName: migrates a fresh file into a private directory with private sidecars
adopts a legacy user_version without re-running its migrations
rolls back the whole pending batch when a migration fails
refuses a file migrated by a newer build
serves two databases from one layer under their own keys
deferred builds the service on the first call, not when the layer builds
deferred retries a failed build on the next call instead of caching the failure

telemetry.testName: emits no statement spans by default while keeping the caller span

features.title: Free pages go back to the disk
features.summary: A new file is created with auto_vacuum = INCREMENTAL, a bounded incremental_vacuum pass returns at most 32 free pages every 5 minutes, and `reclaim` gives every free page back on the store's own connection: incremental_vacuum on an incremental file, or one converting VACUUM on an older file, only when a user asked. `space` reports page and free-page counts and the mode. An existing file is never converted on its own.

configuration.constraints: Applies only to a file with no page yet; an existing file keeps its mode until reclaim rewrites it.
false turns the passes off; a file that is not incremental or has no free page costs one pragma read per pass and no span.

failureModes: reclaim on a file that is not incremental runs a full VACUUM: it blocks the Host for the rewrite and briefly needs the file's size again on disk.
A failed idle pass is skipped until the next tick, never retried in a loop.

verification.testName: creates new files with incremental auto_vacuum
leaves an existing file in its auto_vacuum mode
reclaim converts an existing file with one VACUUM and reports the bytes freed
reclaim on an incremental file frees every free page without a VACUUM
the idle pass returns at most its page budget per tick and records a span

telemetry.testName: the idle pass returns at most its page budget per tick and records a span

features.title: Lock-wait spans
features.summary: A top-level transaction that waited at least 50 ms before its body started (for the store's one connection, or in BEGIN IMMEDIATE for another connection's write lock) records a `sqlite lock wait` span with the file name and the wait; one that gave up with SQLITE_BUSY after waiting records it as failed.

configuration.constraints: 0 turns the span off; a transaction that starts sooner records nothing.

failureModes: Busy waits of statements outside a transaction are not separated from the statement's own time.

verification.testName: records a span when a transaction waits for the connection another transaction holds
records a failed span when another connection holds the write lock past the busy timeout
records nothing for a transaction that starts at once, or with the span turned off

telemetry.testName: records a span when a transaction waits for the connection another transaction holds
